nina (docs): Quick FYI: spotted a mismatch in the /v1/embeddings docs vs examples. OpenAPI currently shows \"input\": [string] (array-only) but our Python snippet and the hosted API accept a single string too. Customers are getting 422s when using single-string examples from older guides. I'll open a PR to clarify and add migration snippets.
diego (sdk-py): Thanks for the catch. Python SDK has a helper that coerces single string -> [string], but Go and some curl examples assume array only. We should document both shapes and make OpenAPI permissive.
rahul (api): We intended the endpoint to accept both. Bug is the generated OpenAPI schema which was tightened to array-only during a previous refactor. Plan: change schema to oneOf: string | array[string] (with x-allowSingle=true for generators) and add a short compatibility note. We also want to add an explicit \"is_batch\" example in docs to show intent.
nina (docs): I will: - update API ref to show two canonical examples (single input + batch of inputs) - add migration section noting that older examples might show array-only - update curl, python, and go snippets - add a small note for SDK authors to prefer single input for interactive calls and array for bulk.
diego (sdk-py): I'll add a patch that preserves existing coercion and add a deprecation warning only in verbose/dev mode if callers pass non-array into the lower-level http helper. Will add unit tests for both shapes. Also will mirror the exact examples from docs in SDK README.
sam (support): We've had 3 tickets this week about \"missing input\" errors when customers copy the curl example from docs and send a plain string. Can we add an explicit \"Common error\" callout in the migration guide (copy/paste friendly)?
rahul (api): Good call. Also update the OpenAPI examples field so codegen won't break (include both examples keys). We should coordinate the deploy with codegen teams: change goes to main, codegen folks will regenerate clients Thursday 02:00-03:30 UTC.
ci-bot: docs preview build failed - YAML lint error in refs/embeddings.md: examples.input: expected array but got string. See preview logs at https://ci.redwood.ai/preview/12345/logs
nina (docs): Fixed the YAML (had an unescaped quote in the python snippet). Re-ran build. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/5678 (WIP).
diego (sdk-py): Quick Q: for the curl example, do we recommend Content-Type: application/json and show both payload forms? I'll mirror exactly.
nina (docs): Yes. I'll include two curl examples: single-string (interactive) and batch-array (bulk). Example payloads below. Please copy them for SDK tests.

nina (docs): ```bash
# single input (interactive) - recommended for one-off calls
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"embed-1.0","input":"What is Redwood Inference?"}'
```

nina (docs): ```bash
# batch inputs (bulk)
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"embed-1.0","input":["Doc one","Doc two","Doc three"]}'
```

nina (docs): ```python
# python SDK (coerces single -> batch)
from redwood import Client
c = Client(api_key=os.environ.get("REDWOOD_KEY"))
# single
resp = c.embeddings(model="embed-1.0", input="A short sentence")
# batch
resp = c.embeddings(model="embed-1.0", input=["one","two"]) 
```

nina (docs): ```go
// go snippet (expects array)
payload := map[string]interface{}{
  "model": "embed-1.0",
  "input": []string{"one", "two"},
}
```

diego (sdk-py): I'll add these exact snippets to SDK tests. Also note for changelog: clarifying OpenAPI to accept both shapes is not breaking.
rahul (api): Confirmed additive change. We'll mark the schema update with x-compatibility:true and add a short note in the OpenAPI description.
ci-bot: docs preview build passed after yaml fix - preview: https://deploy-preview-5678--docs.redwood.ai/ (CI: ✔)
deploy-bot: FYI: scheduling codegen regen for Thursday 02:15 UTC. I'll post an announce in #eng when it's done.
nina (docs): Thanks everyone. I'll merge after SDK unit tests land and add a small "If you relied on array-only examples, here's how to migrate" paragraph. Tagging @diego for SDK test link.
diego (sdk-py): Will open PR for SDK today and link it in the docs PR. Thanks!
